rationales: Corals are marine animals, not the preserved remains of extinct organisms.
Fossils are preserved remains or traces of organisms from the past.
A coral reef is a marine structure, not the general term for remains of extinct organisms.
Endangered describes a species at risk of extinction, not its remains.
Roots mainly absorb water and minerals and anchor the plant.
Stems support the plant and transport materials.
Flowers are the plant’s reproductive organs.
Leaves mainly perform photosynthesis and gas exchange.
“Mala” means bad, as in the phrase “mala aria” (bad air).
“Good” is not the meaning of “mala.”
“Air” is not the meaning of “mala.”
“Water” is not the meaning of “mala.”
Taxonomy chiefly deals with naming and classifying organisms, not their full evolutionary history.
Systematics deals with classification and evolutionary relationships among organisms.
Genetics studies genes and heredity.
Ecology studies interactions between organisms and their environment.
Plant cells generally have a cell wall made mainly of cellulose.
Fungal cells have a cell wall, usually containing chitin.
Bacteria generally have a cell wall, though some exceptions exist.
Animal cells lack a cell wall.
Chloroplasts are green plastids containing chlorophyll.
Leucoplasts are colourless plastids.
Chromoplasts contain pigments that give colour.
Lipids are biomolecules, not a type of plastid.
Karyokinesis is the division of the nucleus.
Cytokinesis is the division of the cytoplasm.
The phragmoplast helps form the cell plate in dividing plant cells; it is not the name for cytoplasmic division.
Phagocytosis is the engulfing of particles by a cell.
Metaphase follows prophase and involves chromosome alignment.
Anaphase follows metaphase as chromatids separate.
Interphase is the period between cell divisions, not the reversal of prophase.
Telophase reverses many events of prophase as the nuclei reform and chromosomes decondense.
Cellulose is a carbohydrate, not the usual chemical nature of enzymes.
Glucose is a simple sugar, not the usual chemical nature of enzymes.
Lipids are not the usual chemical nature of enzymes.
Most enzymes are proteins.
Lysosomes digest cellular materials and are not the main site of aerobic respiration.
The cytoskeleton provides structural support and is not the main site of aerobic respiration.
Mitochondria are the main site of aerobic respiration in eukaryotic cells.
Plastids are not the site of aerobic respiration.
In adults, red bone marrow in bones such as the ribs produces red blood cells.
The spleen filters blood and can store blood cells, but it is not the normal site of adult red blood cell production.
The liver is a major blood-cell production site during fetal development, not normally in adults.
The lungs exchange gases and do not produce red blood cells.
Anatomy studies the structure of organisms.
Genetics studies genes and their role in inheritance.
Taxonomy deals with naming and classifying organisms.
Histology studies tissues.
Sixteen is the expected number of major bio-elements listed in this curriculum.
Fourteen is not the expected count of major bio-elements in this curriculum.
Twelve is not the expected count of major bio-elements in this curriculum.
Ten is not the expected count of major bio-elements in this curriculum.
A. F. A. King proposed the mosquito theory of malaria transmission, but was not the French army physician who made the 1878 discovery.
Ronald Ross later demonstrated the role of mosquitoes in malaria transmission.
Laveran, a French army physician, discovered the malaria parasite in 1878.
Mendel is known for foundational work on heredity, not malaria.
Mushrooms belong to the kingdom Fungi.
Mushrooms are not animals.
Mushrooms are not monerans, a group of prokaryotes.
Mushrooms are not protists.
